A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniUGG research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original UniUGG and encoder evaluations, including spatial understanding, 3D generation, component ablations, and downstream results in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds qualitative generation examples for a simplified model variant in Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: The geometric-semantic encoder, Spatial-VAE, LLM-conditioned diffusion, and spatial decoding procedure are retained. Appendix A.4's simplified direct-token variant matches the existing no-diffusion/no-Spatial-VAE ablation in v1 Table 2, row (d); its expanded description does not establish a new method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is retained across scene generation, spatial/general VQA, Feat2GS, depth estimation, classification, and segmentation. Appendix A.4 adds indoor novel-view examples within the existing generation task, without introducing a distinct dataset, domain, or task requirement.

E2.justification: The matched comparisons retain their encoder, VQA, and generation comparators, including CUT3R and LVSM. The simplified variant and CUT3R already appear together in v1 Table 2; v2 Figure 12 supplies additional visual comparisons using this existing baseline.

E3.justification: The reported training stages, model sizes, data quantities, metrics, and downstream evaluation procedures are unchanged. Both retain a global batch size of 256 and 0.25M held-out generation samples. Appendix A.4 introduces no distinct evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 and Figure 12 extend the existing component ablation with additional scene-level examples comparing the simplified variant with CUT3R and examining its missing visual detail. Earlier projected-image ablation outputs are retained, moving from v1 Figure 6 to v2 Figure 5.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The seed-labeled generation examples already appear in v1; v2's expanded captions do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figure 12 adds qualitative results showing the simplified variant's generated structures and blurred textures. All matched numerical results are unchanged, including UniUGG's VSI score of 40.1 and generation FIDs of 55.01 on ARKitScenes and 55.64 on ScanNet++.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup and substantive loss formulations are retained. v2 cleans up target-latent and teacher-forcing prefix indices to match descriptions already present in v1; these are notation corrections, without new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified 3D understanding/generation, geometric-semantic pretraining, and Spatial-VAE. The claimed 17.9% advantage on VSI-Bench and the stated contribution scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 newly attributes the simplified variant's oversmoothed surfaces and inferior textures to the absence of the diffusion prior and Spatial-VAE, emphasizing their role in high-frequency detail. v1 describes this ablation as suboptimal but lacks this specific failure-pattern and mechanism discussion.

D1.justification: Figure 11 newly documents the existing simplified variant's training/inference flow, including MAE supervision of predicted novel-view ViT tokens. The full model's architecture table, hyperparameters, and promise to release code upon acceptance remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. The From Flatland to Space reference receives a NeurIPS publication update, while author formatting and citation suffixes change; these do not introduce a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and notation edits, numbers sections and appendix subsections, and improves cross-references. It adds an LLM-use disclosure and the simplified-variant explanation, while largely retaining the main narrative and section sequence.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout, extensively resizing and rearranging displays. The qualitative ablation moves into the main text and gains reference images; v1 Tables 6 and 7 merge into v2 Table 6. Figures 11–12 are added, and existing generation panels are reorganized.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.4 and Figures 11–12 make the previously terse simplified ablation easier to assess through explicit supervision details, a pipeline diagram, and visible failure cases. Figure 5 also adds reference inputs to retained outputs. These provide modest gains in clarity and qualitative support, although numerical evidence is unchanged and several retained visualizations become more compressed.
